speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You are presenting with frequent nosebleeds, bleeding from your mucous membranes, and small red spots on your skin called petechiae. To understand the cause of this bleeding, have you noticed if this happens after minor bumps or if it occurs spontaneously without any injury?

speaker: Patient
text: 4-year-old male. The child's parent reports that the child has been experiencing frequent episodes of nosebleeds and has had several instances of bleeding from the gums. Additionally, there have been occurrences of unexplained bruising and petechiae, primarily on the distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given the combination of spontaneous epistaxis, gum bleeding, and petechiae on the extremities, have these symptoms been present since birth, or did they start later in childhood?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Frequent epistaxis. I also have Mucous membrane bleeding, Diffuse petechiae on distal extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Immune Thrombocytopenia (ITP). The presence of mucous membrane bleeding and petechiae without significant trauma or family history of bleeding disorders is characteristic of ITP. I will request a Complete Blood Count (CBC) with platelet count and Peripheral Smear to confirm the diagnosis.
